necessary libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

library(maps)
library(zipcodeR)
```

reading in file. A dataframe is created representing the 1976 spreadsheet
```{r}
grants1976 = read.csv("updatedgrants1976.csv", header = TRUE)
```


We noticed that many rows are duplicates of previous ones. we remove the duplicates here
```{r}
length(unique(grants1976$Grant.Number))
grants1976 = grants1976[!duplicated(grants1976$Grant.Number), ]
```

grant type is either continutation, new, or blank. this sheet is more cleaned so we just set ?s to Xs
```{r}
sum(is.na(grants1976$grant.type))
sort(table(grants1976$grant.type), decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
grants1976$grant.type[trimws(grants1976$grant.type) == "?"] = "X"
```

For award amount, some cells have $ while others do not. For all cells, i am removing \$ so they can easily be formatted in excel later in time. I also found some had a D instead of an \$. I also adjust this. Some cells are a little more difficult in that some values are not picking up (ex: ,050,000 is a cell but there are numbers before).i mark these values with a Y. we also do not touch periods due to previous edits in the file
```{r}
grants1976$award.amount = trimws(grants1976$award.amount)
flagged_vals = grepl("^[,0]", grants1976$award.amount)
grants1976$award.amount[flagged_vals] = "Y"
grants1976$award.amount[grants1976$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub("\\$", "", grants1976$award.amount[grants1976$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1976$award.amount[grants1976$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub(",", "", grants1976$award.amount[grants1976$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1976$award.amount[grants1976$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub("[A-Za-z]+", "", grants1976$award.amount[grants1976$award.amount != "Y"])
numpart = as.numeric(grants1976$award.amount[grants1976$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1976$award.Amount[grants1976$award.amount != "Y"] = as.character(numpart)
grants1976$award.amount[is.na(grants1976$award.amount)] = "X"
```

a few results to observe that my cleaning was successful
```{r}
sort(table(grants1976$award.amount, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

eligible cost is the same. periods are still not touched
```{r}
grants1976$eligible.cost = trimws(grants1976$eligible.cost)
flagged_vals = grepl("^[,0]", grants1976$eligible.cost)
grants1976$eligible.cost[flagged_vals] = "Y"
grants1976$eligible.cost[grants1976$eligible.cost != "Y"] = gsub("\\$", "", grants1976$eligible.cost[grants1976$eligible.cost != "Y"])
grants1976$eligible.cost[grants1976$eligible.cost != "Y"] = gsub(",", "", grants1976$eligible.cost[grants1976$eligible.cost != "Y"])
grants1976$eligible.cost[grants1976$eligible.cost != "Y"] = gsub("[A-Za-z]+", "", grants1976$eligible.cost[grants1976$eligible.cost != "Y"])
numpart = as.numeric(grants1976$eligible.cost[grants1976$eligible.cost != "Y"])
grants1976$eligible.cost[grants1976$eligible.cost != "Y"] = as.character(numpart)
grants1976$eligible.cost[is.na(grants1976$eligible.cost)] = "X"
```
a few results to observe that my cleaning was successful
```{r}
sort(table(grants1976$eligible.cost, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

award amount should be about 75% of eligible cost. we check this below. If this is not fulfilled then award amount is flagged with checkval, since either award amount or eligible cost can have the error. this also flags if award amount is greater than eligible cost; this shouldn't be possible, so if this is the case, it is also flagged with checkval

```{r}
grants1976$award.amount.num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", grants1976$award.amount))
grants1976$eligible.cost.num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", grants1976$eligible.cost))

grants1976$award.amount_clean = grants1976$award.amount.num
x_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1976$award.amount.num))
y_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1976$eligible.cost.num))

numeric_rows = !is.na(x_num) & !is.na(y_num)

grants1976$award.amount_clean[
  numeric_rows & (x_num < 0.70 * y_num | x_num > y_num)
] = NA
grants1976$award.amount_clean[is.na(grants1976$award.amount_clean)] = paste0("checkvals_", grants1976$award.amount.num[is.na(grants1976$award.amount_clean)])
```
we observe our results below. my new values are in the award.amount_clean column
```{r}
grants1976[, c("award.amount.num", "award.amount_clean", "eligible.cost.num")]
```
our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1976$award.amount = grants1976$award.amount_clean
grants1976 = grants1976 %>%  select(-c(award.amount_clean, award.amount.num, eligible.cost.num))
```

everything should be construction for program. will fix below
```{r}
sum(is.na(grants1976$program))
sort(table(grants1976$program), decreasing = TRUE)
```
```{r}
grants1976$program = ifelse(trimws(grants1976$program) == "", "X", "CONSTRUCTION")
```


for CD, we clean up the cells so that they are all numeric. random nonsense is removed. leading 0s are kept. CDs also only go up to 435, so numbers above that will be flagged
```{r}
clean_num = function(x) {
  
  x = as.character(x)
  x = gsub("[^0-9\\.]", "", x)
  as.numeric(x)
}
```

the old CD column is CD. my new, cleaned column is CD_clean
```{r}
grants1976$CD_clean = sapply(grants1976$census, clean_num)
grants1976$CD_clean[trimws(grants1976$census) == ""] = "X"
grants1976$CD_clean[is.na(grants1976$CD_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1976$census[is.na(grants1976$CD_clean)])
x_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1976$census))
grants1976$CD_clean <- as.character(grants1976$census)
grants1976$CD_clean[!is.na(x_num) & x_num > 435] <-
  paste0("incorrect_", grants1976$census[!is.na(x_num) & x_num > 435])
grants1976[, c("census", "CD_clean")]
```

We override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1976$census = grants1976$CD_clean
grants1976 = grants1976 %>%  select(-c(CD_clean))
```

```{r}
sum(is.na(grants1976$step))
sort(table(grants1976$step), decreasing = TRUE)
```


```{r}
grants1976$step[(trimws(grants1976$step) == "?") | (trimws(grants1976$step) == "") ] = "X"
```

For state, we used R's built-in character vector state.abb to match state abbreviations. We also add DC for good measure, PR for puerto rico, VI for virgin islands, and NB, which is what Nebraska was until a later date.
```{r}
sort(table(grants1976$state), decreasing = TRUE)
```
```{r}
states <- c(state.abb, "DC", "NB", "PR", "VI")
grants1976$state_clean <- toupper(trimws(as.character(grants1976$state)))

grants1976$state_clean <- grants1976$state_clean |>
  gsub("0", "O", x = _) |>
  gsub("1", "I", x = _) |>
  gsub("5", "S", x = _) |>
  gsub("8", "B", x = _) |>
  gsub("2", "Z", x = _) |>
  gsub("6", "G", x = _)
grants1976$state_clean <- sub(
  ".*\\b([A-Z]{2})\\b.*",
  "\\1",
  grants1976$state_clean
)

# Validate
grants1976$state_clean <- ifelse(
  grants1976$state_clean %in% states,
  grants1976$state_clean,
  NA
)
sort(table(grants1976$state_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

My new, cleaned column is state_clean
```{r}
grants1976$state_clean[is.na(grants1976$state_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1976$state[is.na(grants1976$state_clean)])
grants1976[, c("state", "state_clean")]
```
our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1976$state = grants1976$state_clean
grants1976 = grants1976 %>% select(-c(state_clean))
```

```{r}
grants1976$ZIP.code_clean = sprintf("%05s", gsub("[^0-9]", "", grants1976$ZIP.code))
grants1976$ZIP.code_clean = ifelse(grants1976$ZIP.code_clean %in% zip_code_db$zipcode, grants1976$ZIP.code_clean, "X")
sort(table(grants1976$ZIP.code_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

For region, we do something similar to CD. however, we also check if the number of characters is over 2. if it is, then the value is incorrect. usually these values were zipcodes
```{r}
clean_region = function(x) {
  
  x = as.character(x)
  reg = regmatches(x, regexpr("\\d+", x))
  if (length(reg) == 0 || reg == "") {
    return("X")
  }
  if (nchar(reg) > 2) {
    return("X")
  }
  return(as.numeric(reg))
}
```

```{r}
grants1976$region_clean = sapply(grants1976$region, clean_region)
sort(table(grants1976$region_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```
my new, cleaned entries are below in region_clean
```{r}
grants1976[, c("region", "region_clean")]
```

our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column

```{r}
grants1976 = grants1976 %>%  select(-c(region_clean))
```

for city, we still use the fuzzy matching method. however, we utilize the zipcodesr package to obtain a list of all cities in the US for matching. Thus, the keywords are now the list of cities from the package
```{r}
cities = unique(toupper(zip_code_db$major_city))
grants1976$city[trimws(grants1976$city) == ""] = "X"
valid_cities = c(cities, "X", "SANTURCE")

grants1976$city_clean <- valid_cities[
  amatch(grants1976$city, valid_cities, method = "jw", maxDist = 0.20)
]

sort(table(grants1976$city_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

We see my new, cleaned entries are below in the column city_clean
```{r}
grants1976$city_clean[is.na(grants1976$city_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1976$city[is.na(grants1976$city_clean)])
grants1976[, c("city", "city_clean")]
```
our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1976$city = grants1976$city_clean
grants1976 = grants1976 %>%  select(-c(city_clean))
```

Now we fix award date. i can notice some dates look to be incomplete. thus i am marking them as incomplete
```{r}
grants1976$award.date[trimws(grants1976$award.date) == ""] = "X"
```

```{r}
clean_date = function(x) {
  
  x = trimws(as.character(x))
  d = as.Date(x, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
  return(d)
}
```

We get dates to all have a similar format and represent the correct date. anything that is ambiguous is flagged
```{r}
grants1976$award.date_clean = sapply(grants1976$award.date, clean_date)
grants1976$award.date_clean = as.Date(grants1976$award.date_clean, origin = "1970-01-01")
grants1976$award.date_clean = format(grants1976$award.date_clean, "%m-%d-%Y")
sort(table(grants1976$award.date_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
grants1976$award.date_clean[is.na(grants1976$award.date_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1976$award.date[is.na(grants1976$award.date_clean)])
grants1976$award.date_clean[trimws(grants1976$award.date) == ""] = "X"
```

```{r}
grants1976[, c("award.date", "award.date_clean")]
```

From project period, we split the two dates to create two new columns: project.start and project.end
```{r}
splitdate = strsplit(trimws(grants1976$project.period), split = "THRU")
grants1976$project.start = sapply(splitdate, `[`, 1)
grants1976$project.end = sapply(splitdate, `[`, 2)
```

with these 2 new date columns, we clean them just like we cleaned the previous date columns. No date listed is marked with an ---, whereas an empty cell is given X
```{r}
clean_date2 = function(x) {
  
  x = trimws(as.character(x))
  d = as.Date(x, format = "%m-%d-%y")
  return(d)
}
```

```{r}
grants1976$project.start = trimws(grants1976$project.start)
cleaned = gsub("\\s+", "", grants1976$project.start)
grants1976$project.start[grants1976$project.start == ""] = NA
dash_only = grepl("^-+$", cleaned)
parsed = sapply(grants1976$project.start, clean_date2)
parsed = as.Date(parsed, origin = "1970-01-01")
grants1976$project.start_clean = format(parsed, "%m-%d-%y")
grants1976$project.start_clean[dash_only] = "---"
grants1976$project.start_clean[is.na(grants1976$project.start_clean)] = "X"
```

my new, cleaned entries are below in the project.start_clean column

```{r}
grants1976[, c("project.start", "project.start_clean")]
```

```{r}

grants1976 = grants1976 %>%  select(-c(project.start_clean))
```

these edits take place after going through the cleaned excel file and filling in all entries for state. we now validate the entries obtained in the city column. we do this through verifying the city in the original city column is part of the state it is in. if it isn't, it is marked as incorrect. if it is, it is left the same
```{r}
tempdf = read.csv("1976progress1 - Sheet 1.csv", header = TRUE)
```

```{r}
tempdf$city_clean <- toupper(trimws(tempdf$city))
tempdf$state_clean <- toupper(trimws(tempdf$state))
tempdf$city_clean[tempdf$city_clean == ""] <- "X"
tempdf$state_validation <- tempdf$state_clean
tempdf$state_validation[
  tempdf$state_validation == "NB"
] <- "NE"

city_state_ref <- unique(
  rbind(
    data.frame(
      city = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$major_city)),
      state = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$state))
    ),
    data.frame(
      city = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$post_office_city)),
      state = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$state))
    )
  )
)

city_state_ref <- city_state_ref[
  !is.na(city_state_ref$city) &
    city_state_ref$city != "",
]



valid_pair <- paste(
  tempdf$city_clean,
  tempdf$state_validation
) %in% paste(
  city_state_ref$city,
  city_state_ref$state
)


tempdf$city_clean[
  !valid_pair &
  tempdf$city_clean != "X"
] <- paste0(
  "incorrect_",
  tempdf$city[
    !valid_pair &
    tempdf$city_clean != "X"
  ]
)

tempdf$state_validation <- NULL
```

```{r}
tempdf[, c("city", "city_clean")]
```

```{r}
tempdf$city = tempdf$city_clean
tempdf = tempdf %>%  select(-c(city_clean, state_clean))
```

we are now officially done making edits for the spreadsheet in R. as we did a very general cleaning, we still need to go into the spreadsheet and manually fix values. we continue this below after downloading our finished product
```{r}
write.xlsx(tempdf, "1976complete1.xlsx")
getwd()
```
